cards.explanation: The answer is compassion, friends. Isaiah says, “For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob…” before anything else happens. The very first thing Jacob gets is the LORD's tenderness. Then the verse says He will once again choose Israel and settle them in their own land.
The answer is True. Isaiah says, “once again He will choose Israel and settle them in their own land.” Hear that "once again"? It's a fresh start for Israel. The LORD isn't done with them.

The answer is False, friends. Isaiah says, “The foreigner will join them and unite with the house of Jacob.” Nobody is shown the door in this verse. The foreigner joins up and stands with the house of Jacob.

The answer is that they make captives of them, friends. Isaiah says, “They will make captives of their captors and rule over their oppressors.” The ones who held Israel are the ones held. Quite the turnaround.

The answer is contempt, friends. Isaiah says, “…you will sing this song of contempt against the king of Babylon…” It's not a gentle tune. It's aimed straight at the king, and it's a song for the day the LORD gives rest.
The answer is the LORD, friends. The song says, “The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers.” No army gets the credit. The One who broke it is the One who gave rest.
The answer is rage, friends. The staff of the wicked “…subdued the nations in rage with relentless persecution.” That's how the oppressor ruled before the LORD broke it. Relentless, rage, no breaks.
The answer is False, friends. The song says, “All the earth is at peace and at rest; they break out in song.” Peace and rest come first, and then the singing starts. The whole earth sounds relieved.

The answer is that no woodcutter comes against them, friends. The trees say, “Since you have been laid low, no woodcutter comes against us.” They have their own reason to sing. Trees who don't have to worry about the woodcutter are trees in a good mood.

The answer is the rulers of the earth, friends. Sheol “…stirs the spirits of the dead to greet you…” and these are all the rulers of the earth. Every one of those kings gets the news that someone new is arriving.
The answer is False, friends. Sheol “…makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.” They don't stay put. They get up to meet him.

The answer is that they say he has become weak like them, friends. The dead kings tell him, “You too have become weak, as we are; you have become like us!” The king who made nations tremble is now one of them. Funny how a throne doesn't come with a warranty.
The answer is destroyer, friends. The song says, “You have been cut down to the ground, O destroyer of nations.” That's the name the song gives him. Cut down, that's how it ends.
The answer is throne, friends. He says in his heart, “I will raise my throne above the stars of God.” A throne above the stars. That's one tall chair.

The answer is to make himself like the Most High, friends. That's the last "I will." He says, “I will make myself like the Most High.” The Most High is God. Then the song says he will be brought down to Sheol (Isaiah 14:15).

The answer is the lowest depths of the Pit, friends. The song says, “But you will be brought down to Sheol, to the lowest depths of the Pit.” He wanted to go up above the clouds. The song sends him the other direction.

The answer is, “Is this the man who shook the earth…” friends. Those who see him stare and ask that question. I bet they can hardly believe it's the same guy. He made kingdoms tremble, and now people just stare.
The answer is False, friends. The people remember him as the one “…who refused to let the captives return to their homes?” He said no to letting them go home. That's the memory that sticks.

The answer is that he is cast out of his grave, friends. The song says, “But you are cast out of your grave like a rejected branch…” The other kings are resting in their tombs, and he isn't. I think this is one of the heavy parts of the song.

The answer is that he destroyed his land and slaughtered his people, friends. The song says, “You will not join them in burial, since you have destroyed your land and slaughtered your own people.” Burial with the other kings is what he doesn't get. The reason is what he did to his own land and people.

The answer is False, friends. The song says, “They will never rise up to possess a land or cover the earth with their cities.” The text says "never," so they don't get to possess a land or cover the earth with their cities.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, “I will cut off from Babylon her name and her remnant, her offspring and her posterity…” declares the LORD. Four things are named, and He says He will cut them all off. That's the LORD speaking in His own voice.

The answer is broom, friends. The LORD says, “I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction…” The tool is a broom, and the word that goes with it is destruction. That word "sweep" gives it away.
